transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AM), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Montgomery Head of ML Ops), Liam O'Connor (Platform Engineer), Daniel Reyes (Procurement)

Summary (auto):
- Renewal discussion for Montgomery Systems with proposed 18-month extension + regional burst capacity in EU and APAC.
- Agreed pilot scope: 2-week dedicated pool soak with traffic replay, focus on latency SLOs and cost telemetry.
- Security & procurement path noted; customer to provide traffic patterns and procurement timeline.

Topics: renewal terms, dedicated capacity sizing, region activation sequence (EU then APAC), security/KMS questions, pilot acceptance criteria, next steps for PO and SOW.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Avery: okay folks, thanks everyone for joining, we know time is tight so we'll run through the renewal proposition and the regional burst plan, and Samir will cover the pilot details, sound good?
[00:17] Priya: yep that works, thanks. quick note, Liam might need to duck at 3:30 for another call.
[00:23] Samir: perfect, i'll jump in on the technical side. quick agenda: sizing recap, pilot mechanics, latency/cost tradeoffs, security callouts, procurement checkpoints.
[00:35] Daniel: for procurement, main ask is can you give us a clear PO line items and lead times - last time the wording was a bit fuzzy and finance stalled.
[00:47] Avery: yeah we'll provide an amended SOW with explicit line items for the dedicated pool, regional activation fees, and the pilot. i'll make sure the pricing appendix is separate so procurement can route it.
[01:05] Priya: ok great. on sizing, our QPS has a big diurnal and weekly spike — percentiles are weird. we saw a 6x spike last month during a campaign. so we need burst capacity that can handle peak 99.9, not just avg.
[01:24] Samir: understood, and that's the reason we proposed a dedicated pool with burst headroom. question on the workload mix: is text-gen heavy, or are you embedding and reranking much of the time?
[01:36] Priya: majority text-gen for chat agents, about 20% embeddings for search. the chat prompts have long contexts, around 800-1k tokens typical. also our avg response size is like 180 tokens.
[01:51] Samir: long contexts will influence memory and kernel selection. the plan we recommended uses a quantized model variant for cost plus an unquantized fallback for 99.9 SLOs. that gives cost savings on steady state and preserves tail latency.
[02:09] Liam: curious — what's the observed tail with the quantized variant? we can't tolerate 800ms spikes on the EU users.
[02:18] Samir: in our lab tests quantized configs have median 65ms and p99 about 320ms on A100 equivalent, p999 sometimes climbs — but with dedicated pool + smart routing and a small unquantized warm standby you can keep p99 under 350ms. caveat: if you have extremely long sequence batches that can nudge numbers up.
[02:41] Priya: ok that sounds promising, but can we run a replay of last month's peak week?
[02:47] Avery: yes, that's exactly the pilot: we'll replay a 72-hour peak window, then a day at baseline, and run a soak. pilot scope is 10k concurrent connections or your peak pattern, whichever is higher.
[03:02] Daniel: what's the expected pilot cost? headcount in procurement needs a figure.
[03:07] Avery: roughly estimate — pilot is covered by the renewal credit, but operational cost is itemized. we'll send a clear estimate in the SOW appendix.
[03:18] Priya: security — we need to confirm KMS integration, audit logs retention, and SOC 2 evidence. also data residency in EU for EU traffic.
[03:29] Samir: KMS integration yes, we support customer-managed keys via common KMS providers. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM with 90/365 retention tiers. SOC 2 type II report is available; i'll attach the latest. on residency, we can route EU requests to EU region and keep logs in-region; tokenization/payload residency depends on whether you use Private deployment.
[03:57] Liam: if we go hosted but route to eu-west nodes, are the encryption keys in region or is that still global?
[04:04] Samir: keys are customer-managed so you can provision them in the EU KMS and Redwood will use the key reference; data in transit and at rest will be encrypted. keys do not leave the customer's KMS scope. some metadata for routing is still global control-plane unless you pick Private.
[04:22] Priya: right. we prefer to avoid full Private at first because of ops overhead, but want assurances around logs and KMS.
[04:30] Avery: totally, many teams take hybrid approach — start hosted with region routing + customer-managed keys, then move to private if you need full control-plane isolation.
[04:43] Daniel: timeline question — we want the renewal executed and pilot started before end of feb if possible. procurement earliest PO date is feb 20, but internal sign off might be earlier.
[04:55] Avery: OK that timeline is tight but doable. we'll target SOW by feb 11, pilot week slot proposal for feb 21, with a contingency week the following.
[05:06] Priya: for acceptance criteria on the pilot: keep p99 under 400ms for EU after routing, no data leakage, and unit-cost delta within 15% of proposed.
[05:17] Samir: noted. i'll capture explicit metrics and alarms in the runbook: p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost per 1k, error rate, and KV cache hit ratio.
[05:29] Liam: do you support prefix caching and per-customer KV caches? our prompts reuse a lot of context so caching helps.
[05:36] Samir: yes — we offer automatic prefix/KV caching; the dedicated pool can be tuned to keep more KV in memory per customer. there's a tradeoff with throughput but for your patterns it's likely net beneficial. we'll include cache settings recommendations.
[05:50] Priya: great. competitors — just so you know procurement will ask why not Anthropic or our in-house GPUs. we need a short comparison doc on reliability and cost advantage of Redwood's routing + batching.
[06:03] Avery: we'll prepare a one-page TEI with rough numbers and two sample scenarios: steady baseline vs campaign peak. can include working assumptions and sensitivity analysis.
[06:13] Daniel: procurement also wants the cancellation/penalty terms spelled out for the 18-month commitment. can that be in the SOW?
[06:22] Avery: yes we'll include termination clauses, ramp schedule, and a 60-day window for amendments. we'll also include a mid-term review at month 9.
[06:31] Priya: one other question: p95 cost — can we get tokenized breakdown per endpoint? we run several routes; some are high-frequency short prompts, others are long generations.
[06:43] Samir: Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns per route; we can create a demo dashboard for you with the sample traffic so you can see expected cost per route.
[06:53] Liam: about region activation order — would you recommend EU first and then APAC? we have immediate customers in EU.
[06:59] Samir: yes EU first minimizes latency for your european customers. APAC can follow after the pilot, and we can stage it as a week-on ramp. each region has provisioning time of 7-14 days depending on capacity.
[07:13] Priya: what's the lead time for VPC/private activation if we decide later?
[07:18] Avery: Private deployments typically take 4-8 weeks for customer-managed networking and KMS handshake; shortest we've done with pre-cleared infra is about 3.5 weeks but that's rare.
[07:30] Daniel: procurement will need a clear milestone schedule for invoicing. can you map invoices to region activation and pilot acceptance?
[07:38] Avery: yes — invoice schedule will be: initial renewal invoice on PO acceptance, pilot ops credit captured as credit line, region activation invoiced at provisioning, and monthly usage as usual. we'll attach a payment schedule to the SOW.
[07:52] Priya: fine. any risks we should call out?
[07:56] Samir: risks: traffic replay fidelity (we'll need raw logs in our expected format), extreme sequence lengths hitting memory, and network egress surprises in APAC. mitigations are in the runbook.
[08:10] Priya: ok — one last ask: can you include an SLA appendix with p99 and p95 latency SLOs for dedicated vs hosted?
[08:18] Avery: yes, we'll include a dedicated SLA appendix. hosted has a different SLO band. we'll be explicit.
[08:27] Daniel: good. let's recap next steps.
[08:30] Avery: recap: Redwood to send amended SOW + pricing appendix and TEI by 2027-02-11; Samir to deliver pilot runbook and perf checklist by 2027-02-18; Montgomery to provide traffic CSV and peak dashboards by 2027-02-15; procurement (Daniel) to confirm PO owner/tablet by 2027-02-12. schedule pilot week proposed feb 21.
[08:55] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:58] Liam: thanks, i'll send the sample logs right after this.
[09:02] Daniel: thanks all.

End of meeting.
